races.name: Spillers Future Champions Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Qitaal
runners_data.note: Regular hold-up horse in form — four places from six recent runs on Good ground and clearly suited by this trip, though Charlie Johnston's apprentice runner Jack Nicholls has only 12 days between runs and needs to execute a clean turn through Tattenham Corner to get a clear run|
runners_data.comment: Qitaal arrives here in fine fettle after a run just 12 days ago, boasting experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 81 marks him out as the one to beat in this field; the chief concern is that he remains winless in his last six starts despite a string of placings.

runners_data.name: Oj Lifestyle
runners_data.note: Oj Lifestyle won over 10f on Good ground and has the best recent form figures in the race from a hold-up position; Jude Fernandes claims 7lb which is significant, tongue-tie is fitted, and the 29-day break looks fine given previous return-to-form efforts|
runners_data.comment: Oj Lifestyle won two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, with a 29-day break leaving him fresh. Carrying 136 lb from stall one, he rates competitive on our figures and commands respect off an official mark of 73.

runners_data.name: Golden Circet
runners_data.note: Jim & Best yard is quiet (0/6 in 14 days) and this horse's best efforts have come over longer trips including a recent second over 16f — the natural hold-up style means it will be doing its best work late, but the reduced trip from 16f to 10f is a question mark|

runners_data.name: Show Biz Kid
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Firm ground so the Good-to-Firm surface is a genuine positive; though instinctively a hold-up type, the small field could see Luke Catton push forward if a gap appears — blinkers fitted and the Birkett yard had a winner 14 days ago suggesting stable form|
runners_data.comment: Show Biz Kid landed a win three starts back but has managed only a third and a fifth since, and ranked fifth of six on our figures he faces a stiff ask here; has run over today's trip and going, and 14 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Magical Merlin
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's runner has been placed four times recently over shorter trips (7-8f) and this step back up to 10f on Good-to-Firm is the key angle; Millie Wonnacott's 3lb claim helps offset the weight, but 59 days off is the longest absence in the field and fitness must be taken on trust|
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in his last five starts — a fourth two starts back and seconds four and five starts back — Magical Merlin brings distance-and-going experience and a rating of 74 that marks him as a live threat, though 59 days off the track is the one question mark.

runners_data.name: Bobacious
runners_data.note: Mark Hoad's yard is almost inactive (0/1 in 14 days) and this horse's form string shows no wins since a handicap mark well below current — natural hold-up style means it will be towards the rear, but a recent third over 10f on Good ground keeps it in contention if the race sets up for a fast finish|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a fifth last time out and no finish better than third in recent starts, Bobacious is hard to fancy at the foot of our rankings; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 14 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: With all six runners carrying a hold-up profile, there is no natural front-runner in this field and the race is highly likely to crawl in the early stages before developing into a sprint finish from two furlongs out on Epsom's rising ground. Qitaal and Oj Lifestyle are the truest hold-up operators and will be content to track the rear, while Golden Circet, Show Biz Kid, Magical Merlin, and Bobacious are all redistributed from their natural positions — the field holds more genuine hold-up types than the pace map can place at the rear, and none of these four can be confident of getting their favoured position in a race where everyone wants to sit in. The most likely scenario is a slowly-run, bunched affair where horses drift wide rounding Tattenham Corner and the race is decided by a sharp, well-timed turn of foot in the final two furlongs. This race shape heavily favours horses with a clean finishing kick and the tactical awareness to find daylight late — a sharp, quick-footed closer who can thread through a bunched field on the run-in holds the clearest advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Bunched Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is dawdling and the race explodes in the final two furlongs with all six converging
scenarios.body: With no horse willing to go forward, the field bunches through Tattenham Corner and the race becomes a two-furlong dash up the straight, rewarding the sharpest finisher over the others

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steadied Then Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If one runner edges reluctantly to the front and sets a crawl, leaving closers with room to wind up from well off the pace
scenarios.body: A lone horse drifts to the lead at a crawl, creating a false-pace dynamic where the true hold-up horses gain maximum momentum into the straight; those who save the most ground through the turn and find a clear run benefit most

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Contested Early Positions
scenarios.trigger: If two or more horses push forward from the gates to secure a prominent pitch, generating genuine early fractions
scenarios.body: A competitive early pace develops unexpectedly, stretching the field and suiting those who can travel prominently without being exposed; Show Biz Kid or Golden Circet, if pushed forward, could exploit a strung-out field

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos Wide Draw
scenarios.trigger: If horses fan wide on the turn and interference forces multiple runners off their intended lines in the final stages
scenarios.body: The undulating Epsom track causes runners to spread across the width of the straight, with those drawn widest losing ground and the winner finding a fortuitous gap on the rail; horses with adaptable riders who can switch lines quickly benefit

watchPoints.text: No horse appears willing to lead — watch the first two furlongs closely to see if any rider is pushed forward by the field walking into the gates, as the horse that takes up the running reluctantly will set the shape of the entire race

Qitaal and Oj Lifestyle are the most battle-hardened hold-up horses in the field; if both find daylight simultaneously on the run from two furlongs out they could dominate and squeeze out the redistributed midfield types

Golden Circet, Show Biz Kid, Magical Merlin, and Bobacious are all mapped to midfield but are natural hold-up horses — watch for crowding and interference through Tattenham Corner if all four are tracking each other on the same inside line

The Good-to-Firm surface at Epsom will put a premium on a quick stride and sharp acceleration — horses whose recent form is exclusively on softer ground (Golden Circet has STA and SOF entries) may find the faster conditions less forgiving up the straight

Apprentice jockeys are riding all six runners — positional errors in a slow-run race where timing the challenge is everything are more likely than in a professional field, making the draw and early positioning in the first furlong unusually consequential

races.name: Spillers EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Out Of This World
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a win over 8f on good ground and a second in the same conditions; lone pace-setter here with no rival to press her, giving her every chance to control fractions — the STYLE_FIT tag reflects she carried a prominent rather than lead tag in her runs, but nothing here is likely to beat her to the front.

runners_data.name: Banged Up
runners_data.note: Has a finishing fade flag and a 0/1 record on good ground; OR=120 mark looks stiff for a two-year-old with one run, and the fact that this horse wants to come from behind but is squeezed into a midfield role by field composition makes it harder for jockey Callum Hutchinson to execute the natural game plan.

runners_data.name: Camarda Rc
runners_data.note: Unraced debutant for Richard Hannon, whose string has been in good form (9/49 in 14 days); going and style are unknown, which creates genuine uncertainty but also the possibility this is a forward-going type who could slot in behind the leader — watch the market.

runners_data.name: Cool King
runners_data.note: One run at Sandown over 6f, finishing seventh; steps up to 7f here for Marco Botti and Neil Callan, with the extra furlong likely to suit, but the hold-up style on a day when the lone pacer controls the tempo is a real concern for his chances.

runners_data.name: Otis Bay
runners_data.note: Debutant for Harry Eustace, a trainer who has good two-year-old form (3/12 in 14 days); completely unknown quantity stylistically, so if he turns out to be a prominent racer this race shape could suit — jockey Jack Nicholls (3) will need to be positive early if that is the intention.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Galore
runners_data.note: Two runs on good ground including a step up to 7f at Goodwood where he finished eighth; the extra furlong trip is not new but the hold-up style in a pace-starved race leaves him dependent on a strong gallop that is unlikely to materialise, which is a structural disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Benefacta
runners_data.note: Best effort was a third over 6f on good ground, but two subsequent efforts on soft have been poor; moving to good-to-firm at Epsom is a change in conditions that could help, yet the horse's natural hold-up tendency is suppressed by the field's composition, forcing a midfield role that is not optimal.

runners_data.name: Aminaty
runners_data.note: Two runs at 7f on good ground both produced poor results (7th and 11th); Andrew Balding's yard is hitting form (7/37 in 14 days) and Daniel Muscutt is a competent handler, but the horse's actual preference to race from the rear is compromised by the crowded hold-up section of this field.

runners_data.name: Secret Flite
runners_data.note: One run, a ninth over 6f on good ground, and carries a finish-fade flag; Tom Ward's 0/9 trainer stat in the past 14 days is a negative angle, and stepping up in distance with a hold-up style in a controlled-pace race makes it hard to construct a compelling winning scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Out Of This World is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pace rival to press her, she is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on good-to-firm ground over Epsom's 7f. The remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up types — Cool King, Whiskey Galore, Secret Flite, Banged Up, Benefacta, and Aminaty all want to come from off the pace — but the map cannot accommodate them all at the rear, and Banged Up, Aminaty, and Benefacta are redistributed to midfield positions that are not their natural home. With one horse controlling the fractions unchallenged, pace will be honest but not searching, and the lack of genuine competition for the lead means Out Of This World can preserve energy deep into the race. This shape strongly favours the lone pace-setter and, secondarily, a horse with one clean tactical kick from a tracking position — true deep closers are disadvantaged here because the tempo is unlikely to be strong enough to bring them into contention from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Pacer Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Out Of This World sets a comfortable, uncontested gallop and the field fails to produce a sustained late challenge.
scenarios.body: Out Of This World dictates every yard, controls the fractions, and simply has to find enough to hold on when the hold-up horses make their move in the final two furlongs; on good-to-firm Epsom turf where she has already shown form, she is ideally placed. Horses sitting just off the pace in a prominent position — potentially Camarda Rc or Otis Bay if forward-going — are the main dangers to her supremacy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse stalks Out Of This World closely from second or third and produces a sharp turn of foot entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A race run at a measured pace over Epsom's undulating 7f will play into the hands of a horse who sits within a length or two of the leader and kicks decisively; Camarda Rc and Otis Bay, both unknown quantities with Unknown going tags, could be forward-going types in disguise who benefit most from this shape. The key is whether their jockeys commit early enough to shadow Out Of This World rather than getting buried in the hold-up pack.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swamp Them
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or Out Of This World overcooks it early, leaving the field bunched and a sprint finish to develop.
scenarios.body: A compressed finish would theoretically bring the genuine hold-up horses — Cool King, Whiskey Galore — into contention if they can find a clear run through a tight Epsom straight; Whiskey Galore has experience at 7f on good ground and Cool King is a lightly raced type whose market move would be telling. However, this scenario is discounted because the pace is not expected to be severe enough to manufacture a truly bunched late dash.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If Banged Up, Aminaty, or Benefacta settle better than expected from their enforced midfield berths and produce a late run.
scenarios.body: These three are genuine hold-up horses mapped to midfield through redistribution and are effectively racing out of their preferred style, which materially lowers their chance in this controlled-pace scenario; even if one delivers, the lack of a strong pace to close into makes it the least likely outcome. This scenario only fires if the race becomes genuinely messy or tactical.

watchPoints.text: Out Of This World (Rob Hornby) has the entire race to herself on the front end — watch whether she is allowed to coast or if Hornby actually kicks on early, as the margin of control she is given will determine whether trackers can ever get to her.

Camarda Rc and Otis Bay are both debutants with unknown styles — if either is a natural front-goer or prominent racer, they will immediately change the pace dynamic and may press Out Of This World harder than the current map suggests.

Banged Up carries OR=120 but has only one race to its name (finishing 16th over 6f) and the finishing-fade flag is a genuine red light — if the market shortens it significantly, that would be the only reason to revisit its chance.

Whiskey Galore steps back to 7f having been beaten eight lengths at Goodwood over the same trip — watch whether Ross Coakley commits earlier than usual given the lack of genuine pace in the race, as sitting too far back on a controlled gallop will leave him without the acceleration he needs.

races.name: Spillers Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Twilight Moon
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse with two recent wins over 12f on Standard, Marcus Tregoning's four-year-old has shown the ability to finish powerfully but those successes came on all-weather; the step back to Good ground (9/15 in similar going) and reliance on Imperial Cult getting caught by the field are the key questions Dougie Costello must manage.
runners_data.comment: Twilight Moon has two wins in her last five starts and comes here with distance-and-going experience, fit enough at 27 days since her last run; the worry is that a fifth last time out suggests she may need things to fall right to recapture that earlier spark.

runners_data.name: Dream Harder
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up type for Mark Loughnane fitted with a hood and tongue-tie, carrying 133lbs and returning from 19 days off; its entire recent form reads as a string of mid-pack finishes on Good ground over shorter trips, and the step up to 14f on fast going asks a fresh question of a horse that has looked in modest form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Dream Harder nevertheless catches the eye as the top-rated runner here, and has run over today's trip and going — his 19-day turnaround looks sharp enough. The 133 lb burden is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Imperial Cult
runners_data.note: Recent back-to-back wins at 11f and 12f on Soft/Standard with a 10f win on Good; George Baker's trainer strike rate of 3/9 in the past 14 days is encouraging, and as the lone front-runner on fast ground with only six days since its last run, it holds the clearest tactical advantage in this field despite a STYLE_FIT tag suggesting it is operating slightly out of its deepest comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: Imperial Cult arrives in fine nick, winning last time out and with three wins in his last five starts — he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 128 lb is no impost for a horse in this form. The sole concern is whether six days is enough recovery.

runners_data.name: Stage Show
runners_data.note: Finley Marsh rides for a trainer with a 1/1 record over the past 14 days, and Stage Show has a legitimate winning run over 12f on Good to its name — its redistribution to midfield reflects the truth that it is a hold-up horse by nature, so sitting closer than usual demands adaptability; the 33 days since its last run and the headgear (p) noted in its profile are worth monitoring for freshness.
runners_data.comment: Stage Show brings solid recent form to this contest — third last time out and a winner three starts back — with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour; the main risk is that eighth two starts back hints at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Two Plus Two
runners_data.note: Ed de Giles's six-year-old wears a hood and has strong place form over 14f on Good, making the trip and going genuinely in its favour; it is a natural rear-of-field type carried forward on the map, so Dylan Hogan will need it to travel comfortably in midfield rather than its habitual position, and the 0/2 trainer record in the 14-day window does not add confidence.
runners_data.comment: Two Plus Two has managed just one win in his last five starts, with a pair of fourths either side of a runner-up effort doing little to inspire confidence — he ranks last on our figures here. The distance and going experience counts in his favour, and 21 days off should leave him fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Imperial Cult is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and, with no genuine rival to press them from the outset, Neil Callan can dictate a controlled, unhurried tempo over Epsom's 1m4f on Good to Firm ground. Behind, Twilight Moon and Dream Harder are both true hold-up horses who will settle at the rear, while Stage Show and Two Plus Two are also natural hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because this field contains more rear-of-field horses than the shape can accommodate — Stage Show and Two Plus Two are most likely to actually secure the closer midfield slots, though neither is operating in their natural role. With Imperial Cult able to roll along at a pace entirely of their choosing and no significant pressure expected until turning for home, this race shape strongly favours a prominent, pace-controlling profile: a lone front-runner on a flat course in fast ground who can conserve energy early and kick clear down the straight is a potent tactical position here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Imperial Cult Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Imperial Cult secures the front and faces no meaningful pressure through the middle mile, allowing a controlled solo display.
scenarios.body: Callan dictates every fraction, the hold-up horses are left with too much ground to make up on fast ground over this trip, and Imperial Cult's recent winning form at 12f on Good stands up under a penalty-free weight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Catch Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves too slow and the trailing group get a strong closing run down Epsom's straight.
scenarios.body: Twilight Moon or Dream Harder, both natural hold-up horses with winning form on similar going, close dramatically if Imperial Cult has used too much energy making all; the flat, straight finish gives closers a real chance only if the pace has been genuinely dawdling.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stage Show Swoops Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If Stage Show, operating ahead of its true natural position, manages to stalk Imperial Cult and pounce in the straight.
scenarios.body: Alexandra Dunn's runner has course-distance form and won over 12f on Good, and if it can sit second through the race it becomes a dangerous stalker; its STYLE_FIT tag means this depends on it adapting well to a position it does not habitually occupy.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Two Plus Two Grabs Late Place
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and Two Plus Two's strong 14f form on Good ground produces a late rattle through.
scenarios.body: Two Plus Two has won and placed multiple times over 14f on Good and carries the lowest weight, but as a genuinely redistributed hold-up type racing ahead of its natural ground, it needs everything to fall right; a place rather than a win is the realistic ceiling in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Imperial Cult (Neil Callan) could exploit an uncontested lead on fast ground — watch whether any runner makes a move to go with it in the first half-mile, because if none do, the race may already be won.

Twilight Moon and Dream Harder are both genuine hold-up horses and could find themselves racing against each other for the same late ground — if both are held up, one may box the other in entering the straight.

Stage Show's last run was 33 days ago; watch for signs of ring-rustiness on the way to post or sluggishness in the early stages, as it needs to be travelling well by halfway to make its presence felt from a non-natural position.

Two Plus Two carries the lowest weight (121lbs) in the field and has excellent course-trip-going form credentials — if it travels unexpectedly well tracking the pace, it could be a bigger threat than its OR of 60 suggests.

races.name: Irish EBF Fifinella Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Chantelle
runners_data.note: Trained by Sir Mark Prescott, who excels placing horses off breaks, but 152 days off is notable and she steps up markedly in trip to 1m½f on Good To Firm — her two wins came at 7f–8f on Standard, so the stamina question is real; she holds the confirmed front-running role and her ability to control tempo is the race's central pivot, though the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence she is running entirely to her strengths today.
runners_data.comment: Chantelle arrives on the back of back-to-back wins, most recently a runner-up effort, and has run over today's trip — a trainer firing at 38% in the last fortnight is a major positive; the concern is 152 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Celestra
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden entry arriving on a sharp 19-day turnaround with solid similar-going form (1W, 3P from 6 runs on Good/Good To Firm variants), giving her a meaningful going profile edge; she wants to race prominently and in a small field should easily slot into second, making her the most natural beneficiary if Chantelle gives any ground in the final stages — headgear (hood/p noted) may sharpen her early focus.
runners_data.comment: Celestra won two starts back and was third three starts back, showing a lively recent profile over today's trip and going; she carries a hefty 133 lb but our rating of 88 marks her clear of this field and she's the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Trio
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 8f on Good going which is an encouraging form pointer for today's conditions, but her true running style is prominent and she has been placed at the back of the map only because the field is saturated with pace-committed types — so her tactical position will be forced rather than chosen, and the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that this makes her task harder rather than easier.
runners_data.comment: Trio arrives here on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making her a genuine threat; the main risk is whether she can reproduce that form under a hefty 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Too Hot To Tango
runners_data.note: A horse with a consistent recent record including a win at 8f on Good and five placings, yet she is a natural prominent racer who will find herself shuffled into a midfield berth by the field dynamics rather than by preference — Hughie Morrison's 0 from 7 runners in the past 14 days is a tepid trainer angle, and the 45-day absence adds mild freshness doubt; racing out of her natural position suppresses her probability despite raw form that reads respectably.
runners_data.comment: Too Hot To Tango won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, making her a live threat at 128 lb; the risk is that 45 days off the track leaves her fitness slightly in question.

races.paceDynamic: Chantelle is the confirmed front-runner here and, in a field of just four, she will stride straight to the lead from the gates with no meaningful pressure to test her — this is a solo-dictating scenario on Good To Firm ground at Epsom over a mile and a half. Celestra and Too Hot To Tango are genuine prominent types who will want to sit close to the pace, meaning the front end of this small field will be occupied early, but neither is likely to attack Chantelle's lead aggressively enough to force a genuinely searching gallop. Trio, though a natural prominent racer redistributed to a hold-up position on the map due to the field's pace-heavy composition, will be last of the four by default rather than by inclination. The field holds more prominent types than can all get their natural position, and Chantelle and Celestra are best placed to actually secure the front two slots, with Too Hot To Tango most likely to be shuffled back against her will. A sustainable, controlled pace set by Chantelle strongly favours horses with tactical versatility who can travel close to the speed and quicken from the front or just off it — prominent runners with a clean Epsom trip profile and good form on similar going hold the clear positional edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Chantelle Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Chantelle dictates an uncontested, metronomic gallop and none of her rivals can manufacture a serious sustained challenge off the turn.
scenarios.body: Chantelle leads throughout at a pace entirely of her choosing, conserving energy through the Epsom bend before asserting from two out; on Good To Firm ground over this trip, a dominant leader who has won over further gets every yard to herself.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Celestra Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Chantelle's long absence (152 days) leaves her slightly flat and Celestra, fresh off 19 days, produces a sharper turn of foot from close range.
scenarios.body: Celestra travels smoothly in second throughout, makes her challenge rounding Tattenham Corner and picks Chantelle off inside the final furlong; her similar-going record of four runs returning 1 win and 3 places underpins the likelihood of a respectable effort.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front end goes faster than it looks and Chantelle ties up in the final two furlongs, opening the door for those behind.
scenarios.body: Too Hot To Tango, though pushed back from her natural prominent position, possesses the recent consistent form (323361) to capitalise if the pace implodes; Trio, similarly a natural front-runner mapped rearward by field dynamics rather than preference, is the least likely beneficiary given both are racing out of their comfort zone.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, All Change
scenarios.trigger: If a false early pace or significant positional scrimmaging disrupts the expected order and the race is effectively reset turning into the straight.
scenarios.body: With only four runners any positional confusion is quickly resolved, making full tactical chaos an outlier, but Trio's most recent win at 8f on Good and Celestra's course experience give them the raw ability to respond if dynamics shift dramatically.

watchPoints.text: Chantelle's 152-day absence is the single biggest threat to her front-running dominance — watch for any signs of greenness or fading in the final two furlongs that would expose the entire pace scenario.

Celestra's headgear (hood) could sharpen her early to the point where she pressures Chantelle more aggressively than expected — if she goes with the leader rather than tracking, the pace dynamic changes meaningfully for the whole field.

Too Hot To Tango will be uncomfortable racing further back than she wants; watch how Rob Hornby manages her in the first quarter-mile — if she pulls hard from a forced rear position she will burn energy she cannot afford over 1m½f on Good To Firm.

With only four runners and a dominant pace figure, the Epsom straight — starting from Tattenham Corner — will be the key moment: any horse still under restraint turning in will have minimal time to close a gap set by a dictating leader on fast ground.

races.name: Spillers Winners Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Koffee And Kale
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile but Michael Bell's 3yo has the strongest similar-going record in the field (7 runs, 4 placed on Good), and Daniel Muscutt's positive record on similar types gives this runner the best credentials to quicken sharply on Good To Firm; 21-day break is straightforward.
runners_data.comment: Koffee And Kale has run over today's trip and going, and our rating puts him clear of this field, but he arrives winless in his last five starts — including a seventh last time out — and the yard is in a lean spell, making confidence measured.

runners_data.name: Eyes Front
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby partners this consistent Rob Hornby-trained hold-up type who has finished in the top five in 9 of 11 similar-going starts without winning, suggesting a reliable but limited finisher — the slow-run 7f here is the most suitable race shape it has faced.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Eyes Front nevertheless catches the eye with experience over today's trip and going, a sharp 14-day turnaround keeping him race-fit, and our rating of 69 suggesting he holds more ability than his official mark of 63 implies — the concern is he must prove he can convert that potential into a finish closer to the frame.

runners_data.name: Credit Forgedd It
runners_data.note: Seamus Cronin takes the 5lb claim on this Dow-trained 3yo, whose true colours are those of a hold-up horse despite the midfield mapping; the 14-day turnaround is tight and the trainer's 0/4 fortnight record tempers enthusiasm, though a placed effort at 7f Good last time keeps it honest.
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in recent starts, Credit Forgedd It returns on a quick turnaround of 14 days, has run over today's trip and going, and carries 131 lb from stall 4 — his rating of 66 marks him as a genuine danger, though he remains yet to win.

runners_data.name: Sun Of Dolly
runners_data.note: Neil Callan's mount has failed to make the frame in any of its six similar-going starts and a course that exposes a lack of finishing kick on Good to Firm will not flatter it; genuinely a closer racing in a race that offers nothing to close on.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Sun Of Dolly nonetheless brings distance and going experience to the table, returns on a sharp 14-day turnaround carrying 130 lb from stall 2, and our rating edges above his official mark — the fourth last time out, however, underlines he needs to find more to threaten.

runners_data.name: Red Moon
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's yard is in solid form (4/19 over 14 days) and Red Moon's win at 7f on Good is the single most relevant piece of form in the race; the hood (p) is retained and if Bass adopts an aggressive, self-made-pace approach on the 30-day freshen-up, this represents the most obvious profile to exploit the vacuum of pace.
runners_data.comment: Red Moon won three starts back but has been below that level since, finishing fifth last time out; he has run over today's trip and returns after a 30-day break, though his rating of 58 ranks him fifth of seven runners here.

runners_data.name: Imagine That
runners_data.note: Henry Candy sends out this hold-up type on a 33-day break, and while the trainer's 2/9 recent strike rate is acceptable, the horse has finished outside the frame in all five turf starts on similar going without placing once — the slow-run race shape does not obviously help.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a string of mid-pack and worse efforts, Imagine That is hard to fancy from sixth in the ratings — though she has run over today's trip and going before, and a 33-day freshener at least means she arrives ready.

runners_data.name: Real Gold
runners_data.note: Remarkable consistency in the placed columns across six recent starts (four consecutive thirds) but all on quicker surfaces than today's official going, and all over 5f-6f; stepping to 7f in a race with no pace is an interesting switch but the 0 wins from 11 similar-going starts is a flag.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts despite a string of thirds, Real Gold has experience over today's trip and going, and 15 days since her last run suggests she's fresh — but ranked last on our figures, she faces a stiff task from stall one carrying 121 lb.

races.paceDynamic: With all seven runners carrying a hold-up style and the going report confirming Good To Firm conditions throughout the evening at Epsom, this 7f contest is set to crawl early before erupting into a sprint-finish scramble from the two-furlong pole. No confirmed front-runner exists in the field, meaning the early stages will likely be tactical and slow, with position jockeying replacing genuine pace-setting. The race will be run in a bunch, drifting into a compressed final two furlongs where a single powerful surge from a prominent finishing position will settle matters — horses who can sit handy without cover and accelerate sharply on Good To Firm ground are strongly favoured. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can genuinely accommodate at the rear; Red Moon, Credit Forgedd It, Sun Of Dolly, Imagine That, and Real Gold are all true closers redistributed to midfield, but with no pace to close on, those with the tactical awareness to press forward early — or whose jockeys adapt quickest — will be best placed; Koffee And Kale and Eyes Front, both rated relatively highly and with better similar-going records, are most likely to secure a workable position from which to strike.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo stays crawling through the first half and the race ignites into a furlong-and-a-half dash, the runner who positions closest to the pace without burning fuel wins.
scenarios.body: With no true front-runner to create genuine fractions, the field will bunch and the race becomes a flat-track sprint from the two-furlong marker, rewarding sharpness over stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Red Moon Strikes Tactically
scenarios.trigger: If George Bass on Red Moon pushes forward to make his own luck off the crawling pace and gets a soft lead from two out.
scenarios.body: Red Moon's winning form at 7f on Good ground is the most relevant recent evidence in the race, and a patient jockey who elects to press on at halfway rather than wait could find this slow-run race plays perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Caught Flat Footed
scenarios.trigger: If one runner breaks the pattern and sets a stronger-than-expected pace, causing hold-up horses who are too far back to get outrun.
scenarios.body: In a field of genuine closers redistributed to midfield, any horse that misses the break or gets shuffled back loses all chance as there is no cavalry charge to hide in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Place Scramble, No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so uniformly slow that five or six horses hit the rising ground in a wall and luck in running determines the result entirely.
scenarios.body: This scenario sees the compressed finish produce a chaotic finish where narrow margins separate four or five runners, with the widest draw or best split in traffic proving decisive rather than ability.

watchPoints.text: Red Moon — if George Bass angles away from the pack in the first furlong and sets his own tempo on the front end, this horse's 7f Good-ground win becomes the most dangerous form line in the race and could steal it from the front.

Koffee And Kale — Daniel Muscutt is capable of switching tactics if the pace is nonexistent; watch for this runner to be produced much earlier than its hold-up label suggests, which would represent the most significant positional shift to monitor pre-race.

Real Gold — four consecutive thirds makes it a consistent each-way proposition, but a step up to 7f for the first time and no wins from 11 similar-going starts means it risks being a place-only runner that flatters with proximity without threatening the winner.

Eyes Front — nine runs on similar going without a win is a bankable negative; if this horse reaches the front two furlongs out it may still find a way to get beaten, but it keeps the field honest and its consistency means it will be placed if the race unfolds cleanly.

Field-wide tactical alert — with seven hold-up types and no confirmed pace-maker, watch for an unusually slow opening quarter-mile; horses drawn widest may benefit from avoiding early traffic in the bunched start and could gain a few lengths of clean air heading into the home straight.

races.name: Spillers Spectacular Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Twirler
runners_data.note: OR 69 prominent runner with a recent win over 6f on Good and three sim-going placed efforts from 15 attempts; Seamus Cronin claims 5lb which brings her in at a competitive weight, and she is the most likely horse to pin Lady Gormire down late if she tracks her closely enough.
runners_data.comment: Twirler arrives on the back of a second three starts back and is well treated on our rating as the top-rated runner in this field, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour; the concern is that her two most recent efforts have been disappointing.

runners_data.name: Lady Gormire
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner with a strong record of placing on Good ground (4/5 sim-going runs placed); T14 of 6/28 shows Michael Dods in decent recent form, and Sean Kirrane should get a clean lead — the key question is whether her OR 69 is good enough to sustain the advantage up Epsom's short straight.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Lady Gormire has been consistently placed — second three times and third once in that sequence — and has run over today's trip and going, while her speed rating of 74 edges above her official mark; the main risk is that elusive win.

runners_data.name: Sugar Sugar
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old with a placed run over 6f on Good and a hood flag (hg:/es) worth noting; Jack Channon's stable is running at 4/19 over 14 days, suggesting live confidence, and her prominent style suits the pace shape if she can improve on her last effort.

runners_data.name: Victor Cee
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who is noted with headgear (hg:p), and his six-run form string of 538753 shows inconsistency that makes him a tough proposition; Tyler Heard on board and Phil McEntee T14 at 0/2 offers little support — his best chance comes only if the pace is genuinely searching.
runners_data.comment:
Victor Cee returns in good time after finishing third last time out, and he has run over today's trip and going before; yet to win in his last six starts, but drawn in stall five carrying 129 lb, his rating of 73 makes him an appealing each-way proposition on conditions that suit.

runners_data.name: Elvetham
runners_data.note: Consistent if frustrating placer with three thirds at 6f on Good in recent history and a blinkered headgear tag (hg:b) to sharpen his focus; Conrad Allen T14 at 0/2 is a cold yard flag, and despite solid sim-going stats (4/15) he remains winless, which is a persistent concern in a race he should naturally suit.
runners_data.comment: Elvetham has been a model of consistency, finishing third four times and second once in his last six starts, and with experience of today's trip and going, the conditions look tailor-made; the concern is he remains yet to win despite those repeated near-misses.

runners_data.name: Mount Mogan
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old returning after 155 days off — that layoff is the dominant concern and needs to be weighted heavily regardless of his previous win; his last five runs are all on Standard/All-Weather, so the step back to Good turf over 6f is an additional unknown, and Laura Mongan's T14 of 0/0 gives no current stable form to lean on.
runners_data.comment: A winner in his last five starts but that came over 150 days ago, and consecutive fifth-place finishes beforehand make him hard to trust; ranked sixth of seven on our figures, though he does bring distance and going experience to the table.

runners_data.name: Harry Brown
runners_data.note: Lively 5-6f form on Good including a recent win at 5f (1/5f/GOO in hist), but his natural style is hold-up — placed in midfield here because the field's rearward contingent is too deep to all sit genuinely last; the style displacement means his tactical chance is compromised, and his best form over 5f rather than 6f adds an additional trip caveat.
runners_data.comment: Has run over today's trip and going, and a win among his last six starts gives him a recent form boost, but fifth last time out and a draw from stall seven on 127 lb make this a tough ask for a 56-rated gelding.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Gormire is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no other horse keen to contest for the lead, she should stride into a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the off on Good to Firm ground at Epsom over 6f. Twirler, Sugar Sugar, and Elvetham will all push up prominently behind her, creating a three-deep chasing pack that will keep the tempo honest but unlikely to savage it. With Lady Gormire able to dictate her own fractions, the race shape sets up for a pace-controlled contest where the premium falls on horses with tactical speed and the ability to quicken from a prominent position in the straight — hold-up runners face the double burden of Epsom's short straight and a pace that is sustainable rather than suicidal. Harry Brown is a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield due to redistribution, as the field carries more rearward types than can naturally sit at the back, but that note serves as caution rather than upgrade — prominent-to-lead runners hold the dominant structural edge here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lady Gormire Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Gormire secures a clean, uncontested lead and sets a measured pace that plays to her strong finishing record.
scenarios.body: She bowls along on Good to Firm ground she clearly handles (0W3P at the highest level of sim-going), and with three consecutive placed efforts including two wins in recent form, she has the fitness and class to hold on as the prominent horses fail to reel her in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Gormire's pace is slightly generous and one of the tracking prominent horses produces a sharp turn-of-foot in Epsom's final furlong.
scenarios.body: Twirler is the most likely beneficiary — she has a recent win over 6f on Good and her OR of 69 gives her class parity with the leader; Sugar Sugar also pressed from behind on her last two outings and shapes as a credible threat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Up Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is faster than expected and Lady Gormire ties up inside the final furlong, allowing a late finisher to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Victor Cee has placed form on Good at 5f and 6f and could find late rhythm if the race is run truly; Harry Brown, though racing out of role in midfield, has the engine to capitalise on a strongly-run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Upsets at Rewarded Price
scenarios.trigger: If the pace fragments mid-race, creating a messy rhythm that scrambles the typical order and benefits a lightly-raced or fresh horse.
scenarios.body: Mount Mogan returns after 155 days off and has a win in his most recent start over 7f on Standard, while Elvetham's consistency (three thirds at 6f on Good) means he rarely runs badly in this type of race.

watchPoints.text: Lady Gormire — if she clears the field by 2+ lengths at the furlong pole unchallenged, the race is likely over; watch her jumping position at the start as any hesitation gifts the contest to the prominent pack.

Twirler — her ability to immediately slot in behind Lady Gormire is critical; if she gets shuffled wide or loses her pitch in the first furlong, her chance of delivering the prominent challenge degrades sharply.

Mount Mogan — 155-day absence combined with a switch from All-Weather to Good turf makes her a significant drifter risk; if she shows any signs of scrubbing along before the turn, discount immediately.

Sugar Sugar's hood (hg:/es) suggests she may be making her headgear debut or switching equipment — watch her in the paddock for any signs of edginess, as a first-time hood reaction can cut both ways at the start.

Harry Brown's trainer T14 return of 0/1 and the horse's redistribution to midfield means Rob Hornby will face traffic from a position that does not suit — watch whether he elects to drop in or push forward at the break, as either choice carries a tactical cost in this race shape.
